name: Le Meridien Bangkok
short_description: A Le Meridien hotel on Surawong Road in Silom/Bang Rak, close to the Chao Phraya riverside and Patpong.
ai_summary: Le Meridien Bangkok sits on Surawong Road in the Silom/Bang Rak area, close to the Chao Phraya river and a short walk from the Patpong night market. Guest reviews are strongly positive on service and cleanliness: the Club Lounge, breakfast buffet, front-desk friendliness, and housekeeping (restocking supplies without being asked) all draw specific praise, and several reviewers rate the overall stay as excellent value. As a Le Meridien property it carries the brand's design and arts-forward positioning within Bonvoy's mid-to-premium tier, in the same general district as W Bangkok but with a different brand character. The most notable watchout comes from at least one Ambassador Elite guest who described elite-status recognition as inconsistent and the front-line response as dismissive -- a sharper complaint than the otherwise-positive review pattern, worth weighing if elite recognition is a priority for your stay.

core_facts.address: 40/5 Surawong Road, Siphraya, Bangrak, Bangkok 10500, Thailand
elite_benefits: Room upgrades for Platinum Elite and above, subject to availability

research_highlights: The Club Lounge, breakfast buffet, and front-desk friendliness draw consistently strong praise

faqs.question: Does Le Meridien Bangkok recognize Marriott Bonvoy elite status consistently?
faqs.answer: Mostly, but not universally -- while most reviews describe friendly, attentive service, at least one detailed account from an Ambassador Elite guest reported inconsistent recognition of elite status at check-in, so it's worth confirming your benefits directly with the front desk on arrival.

faqs.question: Is Le Meridien Bangkok close to the Chao Phraya River?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the hotel sits on Surawong Road in Bang Rak, close to the Chao Phraya riverside and its river-cruise piers, as well as a short walk from the Patpong night market.

reviews.title: Le Méridien Bangkok Hotel Review
reviews.author: Andrew Dobson
reviews.summary: Two-night luxury suite stay at the design-focused Silom property; praises the renovated rooms with circular beds, spa and Japanese onsen wellness facilities, dining venues and central location.

reviews.title: A Royal (dis)HHonor: Le Meridien Bangkok
reviews.author: Ben Schlappig
reviews.summary: Upgraded to a circular 22nd-floor room the reviewer found architecturally interesting but impractical to sleep in; criticizes the gimmicky round bed yet praises the breakfast buffet and value.

reviews.title: Review: Le Méridien Bangkok | Marriott Bonvoy
reviews.author: Jean-Maximilien Voisine
reviews.summary: Executive room booked for 30,000 Bonvoy points; found the renovated hotel well-appointed with quality breakfast and club lounge access, worth the points value despite a steep ~$380 cash rate.

reviews.title: Review: Le Meridien Bangkok
reviews.author: Scott Mackenzie
reviews.summary: Three-night Starpoints stay in a spacious, modern room; appreciated the separate shower and large tub plus attentive service, though room-service breakfast was merely adequate.

reviews.title: Review: Le Meridien Bangkok
reviews.summary: Genuine stay review praising the hotel's artistic design and central Silom location, with spacious light-filled rooms, diverse dining venues and thoughtful service for a contemporary stay.
